reviewNote: Drafted by Claude from the chart for faculty review. Not validated teaching content.
summary: Laparoscopic cholecystectomy at 18 weeks gestation. A well prepared case that tests pregnancy physiology: aortocaval compression (already symptomatic supine), aspiration risk with GERD, CO2 pneumoperitoneum, fetal assessment, and a prior PONV history.

decision.rationale: Second trimester is the preferred window and recurrent colic carries more risk than surgery. OB consult recommendations are in place.

redFlags.evidence: Lightheaded supine with BP 94/58, resolved with tilt.
redFlags.action: Left uterine displacement throughout, keep MAP within 20% of baseline with phenylephrine.

redFlags.evidence: 18 weeks, GERD, heartburn today; sodium citrate pending.
redFlags.action: Sodium citrate within 30 min, RSI with ETT.

redFlags.evidence: Insufflation 10 to 12 mm Hg; target EtCO2 32 to 34.
redFlags.implication: Fetal acidosis with maternal hypercarbia; reduced venous return.
redFlags.action: Adjust ventilation to pregnancy normal PaCO2, low insufflation pressure, avoid hypoxemia.
FHT before and after; no NSAIDs; report contractions.
Ondansetron; dexamethasone is acceptable after the first trimester.

planItems.item: RSI with propofol and rocuronium or succinylcholine
Cefazolin 2 g within 60 min of incision
Acetaminophen and short course opioids, no NSAIDs
